About

I’m a graphic designer based in Cairo with two years of experience making visual content for companies and brands. My work covers brand identity and logo applications, social media design, promotional materials and advertising.

I’ve also worked on digital marketing, content planning and social media management, so I design with the audience and the campaign in mind, not just the layout.

I care about clear communication, attention to detail and consistency, so that a brand looks like itself on every surface it appears.

Selected work

Brand identity projects. More are added as project files become available.

Atelier Safea

Floral brand identity. Burgundy and gold, built for a luxury florist.

Overview

Atelier Safea is a floral brand. The brief was a luxury visual direction that feels consistent wherever the brand shows up, from a logo presentation to a social post to a business card.

  • DisciplineBrand identity
  • DeliverablesLogo and monogram, colour palette, social media design, business cards, packaging and brand applications
  • PaletteBurgundy, mauve, cream and gold

Logo and colour palette

A gold monogram with a mauve stroke, shown with the full palette and usage guide.

Burgundy Dark#5B1F33
Burgundy Medium#7A314A
Dark Mauve#4A2433
Cream / Ivory#F2E8D8
Beige Gold#D8C1A0

Social media design

Promotional posts for the brand.

Business card

Business card concepts, front and back.

Packaging

The monogram and wordmark on a gift box and ribbon tag.

Design rationale

A floral brand sells something delicate, so the identity needed to feel premium without becoming fussy. Deep burgundy sets the mood, cream and beige gold carry the logo and main text, and a soft mauve ties the monogram to the flowers.

The palette has a clear usage guide: burgundy for backgrounds, cream for the logo and main text, gold for secondary elements, and darker tones for accents and shadows. That same system runs through the social posts, business cards and packaging, so the brand reads as one.

Double W

Modest fashion brand identity. Burgundy and gold, from wordmark to storefront.

Overview

Double W is a modest fashion brand. The identity pairs a spaced serif wordmark with gold detailing on deep burgundy, and carries the same look from a business card to a shopping bag to the shopfront.

  • DisciplineBrand identity
  • DeliverablesWordmark and monogram, business cards, shopping bag, storefront signage, location card
  • PaletteBurgundy, gold and cream
  • TaglineModern · Modest · Timeless

Wordmark and monogram

The DW monogram on the card front, the name and tagline on the back.

Bag and location card

A shopping bag with the wordmark, and a card directing customers to the Mansoura store.

Design rationale

For a modest fashion label the identity needed to feel calm and refined rather than loud. Widely spaced serif capitals give the name presence, and gold on burgundy keeps it warm and premium.

Fine line-art illustration, a thin gold frame and the tagline “Modern · Modest · Timeless” keep every piece consistent, and the storefront sign carries both English and Arabic.

Safira Real Estate

Luxury real estate brand and promotional design. Black and gold, from monogram to property campaigns.

Overview

Safira Real Estate is a luxury property brand. The identity uses gold on black, with thin gold frames and widely spaced serif capitals, and the same tone runs through the brand statements, property campaign posts and business cards.

  • DisciplineBrand identity, advertising design
  • DeliverablesLogo marks and monograms, brand statement posters, property and investment posts, business cards
  • PaletteBlack, gold and warm cream
  • TaglineMore than properties, a better tomorrow

Brand statement

The tagline set over dark backgrounds, with the wordmark and monogram.

Property and investment posts

Promotional posts for homes in New Cairo and for investment opportunities.

Business cards

A black card with a gold monogram and a cream card with contact details.

Design rationale

A luxury property brand has to look established before it says anything, so the identity stays with black and gold, thin gold frames and widely spaced serif capitals. The S monogram includes building-like forms, which ties the mark to the product.

On the campaign posts, photography leads and short line-icon lists carry the key facts. The tagline “More than properties, a better tomorrow” anchors the brand statement pieces.

Design process

  1. Understand the brief

    Clarify the audience, the goal and where the design will be used.

  2. Research and direction

    Look at the category and references, then set the visual direction.

  3. Develop concepts

    Sketch and test ideas for logo, layout and typography.

  4. Execute

    Build the chosen concept across every deliverable.

  5. Refine and present

    Check consistency and detail, then prepare final files and presentation.
